entries.name: zero-width-sized-coll-unit-3#0
entries.description: A size-flagged tree whose segregated constant 0 is Coll[Unit] of declared length 3. Rule 1020 raises a ValidationException, the size bit turns it into a degrade, and the tree becomes UnparsedErgoTree: the carrier parses and re-serializes to its own bytes. An implementation without the rule parses the constant instead and round-trips the same bytes — so this entry is green either way, and the UNSIZED twin is what separates them.

entries.name: zero-width-sized-coll-unit-0#1
entries.description: A size-flagged tree whose segregated constant 0 is Coll[Unit]() — declared length 0, so no element is read at all. Rule 1020 raises a ValidationException, the size bit turns it into a degrade, and the tree becomes UnparsedErgoTree: the carrier parses and re-serializes to its own bytes. An implementation without the rule parses the constant instead and round-trips the same bytes — so this entry is green either way, and the UNSIZED twin is what separates them.

entries.name: zero-width-sized-coll-coll-unit#2
entries.description: A size-flagged tree whose segregated constant 0 is Coll[Coll[Unit]] — one outer element whose inner length is 2. Rule 1020 raises a ValidationException, the size bit turns it into a degrade, and the tree becomes UnparsedErgoTree: the carrier parses and re-serializes to its own bytes. An implementation without the rule parses the constant instead and round-trips the same bytes — so this entry is green either way, and the UNSIZED twin is what separates them.

entries.name: zero-width-sized-coll-tuple-unit-unit#3
entries.description: A size-flagged tree whose segregated constant 0 is Coll[(Unit, Unit)] — one element, a tuple of two zero-width items. Rule 1020 raises a ValidationException, the size bit turns it into a degrade, and the tree becomes UnparsedErgoTree: the carrier parses and re-serializes to its own bytes. An implementation without the rule parses the constant instead and round-trips the same bytes — so this entry is green either way, and the UNSIZED twin is what separates them.

entries.name: zero-width-unsized-coll-unit-3#4
entries.description: The same Coll[Unit] of declared length 3 in an UNSIZED tree (no size bit). There is no degrade path, so the ValidationException surfaces as a SerializerException and the carrier is REJECTED. An implementation that accepts a zero-width collection parses it and round-trips: the over-accept.

entries.name: zero-width-control-coll-tuple-unit-int#5
entries.description: Negative control: a size-flagged tree whose constant 0 is Coll[(Unit, Int)] — one element (Unit, Int 5); the tuple is NOT wholly zero-width, so the rule does not fire. The tree PARSES — it does not degrade — so an implementation that over-applies the rule rejects this and the family catches it.

entries.name: zero-width-control-bare-unit#6
entries.description: Negative control: a size-flagged tree whose constant 0 is a bare SUnit constant — not a collection element, so the rule does not reach it. The tree PARSES — it does not degrade — so an implementation that over-applies the rule rejects this and the family catches it.

entries.name: zero-width-register-coll-unit-3#7
entries.description: Coll[Unit] of declared length 3 as a box register R4, not inside a tree. It is read by CoreDataSerializer outside deserializeErgoTree's try, so the ValidationException escapes and the carrier is REJECTED with no degrade. An implementation without the rule accepts it.
